problem: Roth's theorem in [N] (Bloom-Sisask 2023, the Kelley-Meka exposition and refinement)
pair_kind: control pair -- BOTH halves are must-not-fire, so nothing is being discriminated

board.name: density increment with Bohr sets -- THE SAME BOARD AS CONTROL 15
board.M: Hoelder lifting, unbalancing, dependent random choice, almost-periodicity -- Kelley-Meka's own five steps, with the ad hoc iteration over high-dimensional progressions replaced by classical Bohr set machinery.

what_happened: Days after Kelley-Meka, the same board was re-presented so that the whole argument runs on classical Bohr set techniques, and two exponent improvements were announced on it: 1/12 -> 1/9 by modifying the almost-periodicity step, and 5/41 after a longer technical optimisation. The authors are explicit about the scope of the change: 'It must be made clear, however, that our sole contribution is at the technical level, allowing the Bohr set machinery to run a little more smoothly; all of the main ideas are the same as in [14].'
tests_for: False board-change alarms on BETTER PLAY BY A SECOND TEAM IN THE SAME SEASON. Control 15 tests that a diagnostic does not fire on the headline advance; this tests that it does not fire on the refinement that followed it, on the same problem, on the same board, weeks later.

why_it_is_a_pair_and_what_the_pair_can_m.what_it_can: SPECIFICITY INSIDE ONE PROBLEM-PERIOD. A rater or a rule that fires on either half is firing on better play, and cannot blame the confound that makes cross-problem comparisons useless (D25: a rater only has to name the problem -- here naming it separates nothing, because both halves are the same problem in the same season).
why_it_is_a_pair_and_what_the_pair_can_m.what_it_CANNOT: DISCRIMINATION. There is no 'which is which' to score: both halves are must-not-fire, so a rater declining to fire twice scores 2/2 by doing nothing. It therefore does NOT count toward the five discrimination pairs that tools/pair_power.py says are needed. See PAIRS.md.
why_it_is_a_pair_and_what_the_pair_can_m.the_asymmetry_to_declare: This half is a LOW-STAKES advance -- an exposition with announced improvements -- while every other item in P1 is a headline result. A rater could in principle separate the halves by prominence rather than by mechanism. That does not matter for a control pair, where no separation is asked, but it would matter if this item were ever reused inside a discrimination pair, and it is recorded here so that it cannot be reused without the caveat.
why_it_is_a_pair_and_what_the_pair_can_m.under_anonymisation: Checked with tools/pack.py --set controls --anonymise: stripped of names, the two halves are nearly the same item -- both read 'a 3AP-free subset of [N]' with a '[name] increment' invariant, differing only in the move slot. For a control pair that is the right property, since both must not fire. It also gives a free noise reading: a rater who fires on one half and not the other, on items this close, is reporting noise rather than a distinction.

not_added_to_the_scored_set: This item is deliberately NOT added to p3-taxonomy/diagnostics.json's item list. Adding it would move a published 2x2, and D25 has already established that no retrospective 2x2 in this tree may be quoted as evidence that a diagnostic works -- so the change would perturb a number that carries no weight anyway. It is encoded as an ITEM, for raters and for the pair structure, not as a score.
